# clio backup create

Snapshot the store into one owner-only archive: a SQLite store is a compacted, transactionally consistent copy (one VACUUM INTO, logically equivalent, never a byte-for-byte clone, and it does not retain deleted pages); a Postgres store is a row-level dump in COPY text format, whose schema is owned by this build; --keep N then prunes the backup directory to the newest N (nothing without --confirm); exit 3 means pruning could not remove every candidate

## Usage

```
clio backup create [--db PATH] [--backend sqlite|postgres] [--label TEXT] [--note TEXT] [--keep N] [--confirm] [--dry-run] [--output json|text]
```

## Description

a SQLite store is read once into a compacted, transactionally consistent copy (one VACUUM INTO, logically equivalent, never a byte-for-byte clone, and it does not retain deleted pages); a Postgres store is read in one repeatable-read transaction into a row-level dump in COPY text format, whose schema is owned by this build, so restoring it needs a target this build created. Either way the archive holds key material when a key-store file exists, so keep it owner-only. --dry-run writes nothing. --keep N then runs `clio backup prune --keep N` over the backup directory, with the same rule: without --confirm it reports what it would delete and deletes nothing

## Options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--db PATH` | text |  | Overrides the store address that `db_target::resolve_target` opens; config and environment decide it when absent. |
| `--backend sqlite\|postgres` | enum: sqlite, postgres |  | Selects the store backend that `db_target::resolve_target` hands to the resolver; config or the address decides it when absent. |
| `--label TEXT` | text |  | Names the snapshot in its manifest; `backup_create_cli::take_snapshot` stores it with the archive. |
| `--note TEXT` | text |  | Records an operator note in the archive's manifest; `backup_create_cli::take_snapshot` stores it. |
| `--keep N` | uint |  | Runs `clio backup prune --keep N` after a successful create; `backup_create_cli` refuses `0` and a value that is not a count. |
| `--confirm` |  |  | Lets the `--keep` prune delete; `backup_create_cli::confirm_needs_keep` refuses it with no `--keep` because a create deletes nothing else. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Prints the plan and writes nothing; `backup_create_cli::dry_run` reports the sizes and the existing snapshot count. |
| `--output json\|text` | enum: json, text |  | Selects the output mode that `cli_output::resolve_output` returns; the terminal decides it when absent. |

## Global options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--bank BANK` | text |  | Scopes the command to one bank; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and the write scope defaults to `default`. |
| `--actor ACTOR` | text |  | Names the acting identity; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and `auth_cli` reads it for the actor commands. |
| `--no-input` |  |  | Refuses interactive input; `backup_restore_cli` treats a run with it as non-interactive. |
| `--yes` |  |  | Answers yes to the destructive-confirmation gate that `cli_confirm::confirmed` applies. |

## Examples

Snapshot the SQLite store under a manifest label.
```
clio backup create --db ./memory.db --label nightly
```

Report the plan and write nothing.
```
clio backup create --db ./memory.db --dry-run
```

Snapshot, then prune to the newest three.
```
clio backup create --db ./memory.db --keep 3 --confirm
```
